migration.migration_reason: Preserved paid Language Quality findings were independently re-adjudicated against the current fixed five-component design rubric. Legacy normalized scores were retained only for audit and were not used to derive component levels. The snapshot is bound to exact source evidence and the current validator recomputes scores.

recertifier.provider_model_provenance_claim: No Anthropic/Sonnet call is claimed for these reconstructed judgments.

component_findings.actionability: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Messages normally provide enough precise information to correct the issue without requiring unrelated guesswork; suggested fixes count only when semantically reliable. Evidence basis: Reviewed adversarial corpus programs probing edge/error conditions (overflow, deep recursion, invalid input) and Python's native error/exception reporting model. | Python raises runtime exceptions with tracebacks including file/line and call-stack context (ZeroDivisionError, RecursionError for ADV-21_depth10000.py-style deep recursion, ValueError from float(input()) parsing as in ADV-05_R.py). | No static type checker in core language; mypy/pyright are external tools (Ecosystem, not counted here); many error classes only caught at runtime. | Tracebacks are clear (type, message, call chain) aiding debuggability, but lack of static analysis means bugs surface late. | ctypes-based overflow simulation (ADV-05_R.py) shows silent wraparound with minimal diagnostics unless explicitly inspected; native Python ints are arbitrary precision so overflow is largely avoided by design except via explicit fixed-width interop. | Deep recursion (ADV-21_depth10000.py) triggers RecursionError with stack trace via a blunt global recursion-limit safety net rather than a structured static diagnostic.

metric.diagnostics.limitations: Comparison-language reprojection requires the preserved paid source evidence plus the historical program/workload/toolchain inputs to match the current shard; mismatches remain misses.
metric.diagnostics.selection_rule: Judge built-in compiler/checker/runtime diagnostic design from normal language use; do not count external IDE/debugger maturity.

component_findings.abstraction_reuse: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Functions, modules/types and generic/polymorphic abstraction support reusable composition across ordinary programs. Evidence basis: Qualitative review of assigned Python micro (mb00-mb11) and adversarial (ADV-01..26) program corpus under /quidra-benchmark/template/programs/python, scored against idiomatic-best-practice rubric per language_quality.md section 7. | Python offers very high functionality/expressiveness: dynamic typing, comprehensions, generators, closures, decorators, multiple inheritance, operator overloading, rich stdlib (itertools, functools, collections, ctypes as used in ADV-05_R.py) enable concise implementations of numeric and adversarial edge-case workloads. | Adversarial corpus (ADV-05_R.py ctypes.c_int32 controlled overflow, ADV-21 deep recursion variants) shows Python expresses low-level bit-width/recursion behavior via stdlib rather than native language primitives. | Micro-benchmark set mb00-mb11 covers control flow, data structures, arithmetic, string/IO with idiomatic comprehensions/unpacking/f-strings, indicating strong expressiveness-per-line. | Weaknesses vs statically typed languages: no native compile-time generics/ADTs, weaker exhaustiveness checking, runtime duck typing reduces structural guarantees.
